rules.explanation: Intermediate build products Xcode writes while compiling each project. They are large, machine-local, and not part of your source tree.
rules.consequence: The next build of each affected project will be a full rebuild and take longer. Source code, git history, and archives are not touched.
rules.howItComesBack: Open the project in Xcode and build. DerivedData is recreated automatically.

rules.explanation: Clang's shared module cache used to speed up compilation of imported modules across projects. It is regenerated on the next compile.
rules.consequence: The first few builds after removal compile modules from scratch. No project settings or source files are affected.
rules.howItComesBack: Xcode recreates ModuleCache.noindex the next time a target imports a module.

rules.explanation: Content-addressed cache of tarballs npm has already downloaded. It exists only to avoid re-fetching packages from the registry.
rules.consequence: The next npm install re-downloads packages that were only in this cache. package.json and node_modules in your projects are not modified.
rules.howItComesBack: Run npm install in a project; npm repopulates _cacache from the registry.

rules.explanation: pnpm's global content-addressable store. Project node_modules directories hardlink or copy from here rather than duplicating every package.
rules.consequence: Projects using pnpm will re-fetch packages on the next install. Existing project lockfiles are not changed.
rules.howItComesBack: Run pnpm install; the store is rebuilt from the registry as needed.

rules.explanation: Offline cache of packages Yarn has already fetched. Classic Yarn and Yarn Berry keep this in different locations; both are regenerable.
rules.consequence: The next yarn install downloads packages again. Your repository lockfile and source are untouched.
rules.howItComesBack: Run yarn install. Yarn restores the cache from the registry.

rules.explanation: Compressed crate files Cargo downloaded from crates.io (or another registry). The src/ checkout of those crates lives beside this cache.
rules.consequence: The next cargo build that needs a crate will re-download it. Cargo.lock and your crate sources are not modified.
rules.howItComesBack: Run cargo build or cargo fetch; the registry cache is filled again.

rules.explanation: Downloaded dependencies, generated jars, and transform caches Gradle uses so subsequent builds do not hit the network.
rules.consequence: The next Gradle build re-downloads and re-transforms dependencies. Project source and gradle.properties are not touched.
rules.howItComesBack: Run the Gradle build; caches are restored from configured repositories.

rules.explanation: Local copy of artifacts Maven has resolved. It is a cache, not your project's source or the remote repository.
rules.consequence: The next mvn invocation re-downloads missing artifacts. pom.xml files are not modified.
rules.howItComesBack: Run mvn package or mvn dependency:resolve; artifacts return to ~/.m2/repository.

rules.explanation: Downloaded pod specs and source archives CocoaPods keeps so pod install does not re-fetch every dependency.
rules.consequence: The next pod install re-downloads pods. Your Podfile and Podfile.lock stay in place.
rules.howItComesBack: Run pod install; CocoaPods rebuilds this cache from the spec repos.

rules.explanation: Cloned package checkouts and build artifacts SwiftPM stores outside your project so packages are reused across Xcode projects.
rules.consequence: The next Xcode or swift build that needs a package will re-clone it. Package.swift manifests are not changed.
rules.howItComesBack: Resolve packages in Xcode or run swift package resolve.

rules.explanation: Downloaded bottle archives and source tarballs Homebrew keeps after installs and upgrades. Installed kegs live in the Homebrew prefix, not here.
rules.consequence: The next brew install or upgrade re-downloads bottles. Already-installed formulae keep working.
rules.howItComesBack: brew install or brew fetch restores downloads. brew cleanup is the Homebrew-native way to prune this cache.

rules.explanation: Per-app caches under ~/Library/Caches. macOS and apps are expected to recreate this data. Individual subfolders are classified separately when a more specific rule matches.
rules.consequence: Apps may launch slower once while they rebuild caches. Documents, photos, and application support files are not in this folder.
rules.howItComesBack: Launch the app. Caches are recreated on demand.

rules.explanation: Diagnostic log files written by apps in your home library. They are useful for debugging and otherwise safe to move to Trash.
rules.consequence: You lose historical log output that might have helped diagnose a past crash. Running apps will start new log files.
rules.howItComesBack: Apps append new logs as they run. There is no restore of old log text.

rules.explanation: Archived builds created by Product → Archive. These are the artifacts you submit to App Store Connect or export as IPAs.
rules.consequence: You cannot re-export or re-submit that exact build without archiving again. Source is not deleted, but the archived binary is.

rules.explanation: Symbol files copied from physical devices you have plugged in. Xcode uses them to symbolicate crash logs for that OS version.
rules.consequence: Crash symbolication for those device OS versions will fail until the device is connected again. Debugging currently attached devices still works after a resync.
rules.howItComesBack: Plug the device in and let Xcode copy DeviceSupport again.

rules.explanation: Simulator device data — installed apps, keychain, photos, and runtime state for each simulated iPhone or iPad.
rules.consequence: Simulator apps and their local data are gone. You will need to reinstall test apps onto new simulator devices.
rules.howItComesBack: Xcode → Window → Devices and Simulators can recreate devices. xcrun simctl delete unavailable is the recommended way to drop dead runtimes.

rules.explanation: Placeholder rule for cargo target directories. v1 does not scan or offer them for cleanup because an active build tree may live here.
rules.consequence: Deleting an in-use target directory can break a running build. DiskPrune therefore never selects this path in v1.
rules.howItComesBack: cargo build recreates target/ inside the crate, not necessarily at this path.

rules.explanation: Machine-wide logs outside your home folder. Trash will usually fail here without Full Disk Access and elevated privileges; that failure is reported honestly.
rules.consequence: Diagnostic history for system services is lost if removal succeeds. Most users will see a permission failure on this item instead.
rules.howItComesBack: macOS continues writing new logs. Old rotated logs are not recreated.

rules.explanation: Sandbox containers for Mac App Store and sandboxed apps. They can hold documents, caches, and settings the app treats as its home directory.
rules.consequence: The app may lose its local documents, login sessions, and settings. Some apps recreate an empty container; some appear to 'forget' the user.

rules.explanation: Support files apps store next to — not inside — their documents: databases, support resources, and offline data. Not the same as Caches.
rules.consequence: Apps may lose offline data, local databases, or license files they stored here. This is why the item is review, not safe.

rules.explanation: The sparse virtual disk that holds images, containers, and volumes. It does not shrink when you delete containers; Docker-native prune commands do.
rules.consequence: Deleting this file destroys every image, container, and volume. DiskPrune never offers it as a cleanup target, running or stopped.

rules.explanation: Local Time Machine snapshots macOS keeps for restore. DiskPrune lists them with tmutil; this rule does not match the whole volume and is never a cleanup candidate.
rules.consequence: Deleting snapshots yourself with tmutil removes local restore points. DiskPrune does not do this and does not offer a button for it.

rules.explanation: The Documents folder is user data. DiskPrune will never offer it for cleanup, even if a nested cache rule exists elsewhere. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Desktop items are user data and visible files. They are never cleanup candidates. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Downloads holds files you chose to keep. DiskPrune never plans this folder. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Photos libraries and pictures live here. This path is unconditionally protected. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Movie files are user data. DiskPrune never offers this folder for cleanup. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Music libraries are user data. This path cannot appear in a cleanup plan. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: iCloud Drive data. Removing it can delete cloud-synced documents on this Mac and beyond. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Password keychains. DiskPrune never scans this as a cleanup target. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: iMessage and SMS history. Protected so a cache clean cannot take conversations with it. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Apple Mail data. Protected; mailboxes are not caches. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Photos library support files. Protected so a library cannot be planned as cache. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Device backups. Losing them means you cannot restore an iPhone or iPad from this Mac. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Private keys and known_hosts. Never a cleanup candidate. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: OpenPGP private keys and trust database. Protected unconditionally. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: AWS configuration and credentials. DiskPrune will not plan this directory. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: gcloud credentials and configuration. Protected so a cache rule cannot reach it. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: The signed system volume. DiskPrune never enumerates this as a cleanup root. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Apple-shipped support files. Not user-deletable cache. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: System databases including TCC. Interfering here can break privacy prompts and more. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.

rules.explanation: Installed applications. Bundles are never cleanup candidates; this path is also deny-listed. DiskPrune classifies this location as protected.
rules.consequence: DiskPrune will refuse to put this path in a cleanup plan. There is no override in v1.
